thought_title: Christian food only; heresy is poison in sweet wine

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, οὐκ ἐγώ, ἀλλ’ ἡ ἀγάπη Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: μόνῃ τῇ χριστιανῇ τροφῇ χρῆσθε, ἀλλοτρίας δὲ βοτάνης ἀπέχεσθε, ἥτις ἐστὶν αἵρεσις: [2] οἳ ἑαυτοῖς παρεμπλέκουσιν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καταξιοπιστευόμενοι, ὥσπερ θανάσιμον φάρμακον διδόντες μετὰ οἰνομέλιτος, ὅπερ ὁ ἀγνοῶν ἡδέως λαμβάνει ἐν ἡδονῇ κακῇ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν.
pass_a_gloss: I urge you, then, not I but the love of Jesus Christ: use only Christian food, and keep away from a foreign plant, which is heresy. These people weave Jesus Christ in with themselves, making themselves seem trustworthy, like people who give a deadly drug with honeyed wine, which the one who does not know gladly takes, and in evil pleasure takes his death.
pass_b_english: So I urge you, or rather not I, but the love of Jesus Christ urges you: eat only Christian food, and keep clear of every foreign plant. That plant is heresy.

Such people blend Jesus Christ in with themselves, putting on a show of trustworthiness. They are like poisoners who serve a deadly drug in sweet wine. The one who does not know drinks it down with pleasure, and with that evil pleasure swallows his own death.

choices.term: οὐκ ἐγώ, ἀλλ' ἡ ἀγάπη Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
choices.english: or rather not I, but the love of Jesus Christ urges you
choices.why: Pauline self-correction (cf. Galatians 2:20 pattern); 'urges you' repeats the verb so the English stands.
βοτάνη = plant/weed, set against Christian food; 'foreign' = belonging to another.
rejected: herbage of a different kind (ANF; stiff)

choices.english: putting on a show of trustworthiness
choices.why: Rare verb: to pass oneself off as credible. Lake: 'simulating trustworthiness'.
rejected: speaking things unworthy of credit (ANF; reverses the sense)

choices.why: Honeyed wine; 'sweet wine' names its point (masking the poison) in one phrase.

anf_compare.notes: ANF 'mix up Jesus Christ with their own poison' follows Lightfoot's conjecture (καὶ ἰῷ), and 'speaking things which are unworthy of credit' reverses καταξιοπιστευόμενοι (posing as credible). Lake prints οἳ ἑαυτοῖς παρεμπλέκουσιν; translated as printed.

notes: Lake apparatus at 6.2: text clearly corrupt; οἳ ἑαυτοῖς παρεμπλέκουσιν implied by SA; G(L) οἱ καιροὶ παρεμπλέκουσιν; g καὶ τὸν ἰὸν προσπλέκοντες; Lightfoot conjectures καὶ ἰῷ παρεμπλέκουσιν ('they mingle poison with Jesus Christ').
Apparatus at end: κακῇ L; om. SA; G κἀκεῖ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ('and therein is death').
'poisoners' in Pass B renders the participle διδόντες with the poison image already in θανάσιμον φάρμακον; no new claim.

review.notes: Checked the single source paragraph against both passes. Greek 'Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, οὐκ ἐγώ, ἀλλ’ ἡ ἀγάπη Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ' is kept in A 'I urge you, then, not I but the love of Jesus Christ' and in B 'So I urge you, or rather not I, but the love of Jesus Christ urges you' (verb ellipsis supplied, agency not reversed). 'μόνῃ τῇ χριστιανῇ τροφῇ χρῆσθε, ἀλλοτρίας δὲ βοτάνης ἀπέχεσθε, ἥτις ἐστὶν αἵρεσις' matches A 'use only Christian food, and keep away from a foreign plant, which is heresy'; B 'eat' and 'every foreign plant' stay within the generic prohibition and do not reverse μόνῃ or the plant=heresy identification. Section [2] 'οἳ ἑαυτοῖς παρεμπλέκουσιν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καταξιοπιστευόμενοι, ὥσπερ θανάσιμον φάρμακον διδόντες μετὰ οἰνομέλιτος, ὅπερ ὁ ἀγνοῶν ἡδέως λαμβάνει ἐν ἡδονῇ κακῇ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν' is preserved in A 'weave Jesus Christ in with themselves... deadly drug with honeyed wine... gladly takes, and in evil pleasure takes his death' and in B 'blend Jesus Christ in with themselves... deadly drug in sweet wine... with pleasure... evil pleasure... death'. The ignorant one remains the taker; οὐκ ἐγώ is not undone; notes disclose the corrupt 6.2 reading. No quoted scripture in the locked text.

Paragraph 1 of the Locked Greek is fully rendered in both Pass A and Pass B. All clauses are present: the exhortation (not from Ignatius but from Christ's love), the command to use only Christian food and abstain from foreign plant (heresy), the description of those who mix Christ with themselves to appear trustworthy, and the simile of giving deadly drug with honeyed wine that the ignorant gladly take, leading to evil pleasure in taking death. Pass A gloss captures the sense: 'I urge you, then, not I but the love of Jesus Christ: use only Christian food, and keep away from a foreign plant, which is heresy. These people weave Jesus Christ in with themselves, making themselves seem trustworthy, like people who give a deadly drug with honeyed wine, which the one who does not know gladly takes, and in evil pleasure takes his death.' Pass B English splits into two sentences but preserves all meaning: 'So I urge you, or rather not I, but the love of Jesus Christ urges you: eat only Christian food, and keep clear of every foreign plant. That plant is heresy.' and 'Such people blend Jesus Christ in with themselves, putting on a show of trustworthiness. They are like poisoners who serve a deadly drug in sweet wine. The one who does not know drinks it down with pleasure, and with that evil pleasure swallows his own death.' No omission, addition, or contradiction. Negation in 'οὐκ ἐγώ, ἀλλ’ ἡ ἀγάπη' is preserved in both ('not I but the love' / 'or rather not I, but the love ... urges you'). Agency is clear: Christ's love urges, the false teachers act. Modality of urging is maintained. Doctrine: the contrast between Christian food and heretical 'foreign plant' is preserved. Scripture: no inline biblical citations in the source, so scripture check is vacuously satisfied. Title 'Christian food only; heresy is poison in sweet wine' names the thought, not just the locus. Notes disclose OCR corruption and variant readings appropriately. All checks pass.
